questions.prompt: A bottle of water has holes at three heights. Which hole squirts water the furthest?
questions.explain: Liquid pressure increases with depth, so the bottom hole has the greatest pressure.

questions.prompt: Why are dam walls built thicker at the bottom?
options: Water pressure is greatest at the bottom
questions.explain: The deeper the water, the higher the pressure on the wall.

questions.prompt: Which statements about liquid pressure are TRUE? Choose all that apply.
options: It is bigger in denser liquids at the same depth
It depends on the shape of the container
questions.explain: Liquid pressure depends on depth and density, acts in all directions, and doesn’t depend on container shape.

questions.prompt: When you drink through a straw, what actually pushes the juice up?
options: Your sucking pulls the juice up
The air pressure on the juice surface pushes it up into the low-pressure straw

feedback.0: Sucking only lowers the pressure inside the straw. The outside air pressure does the pushing!

questions.explain: Atmospheric pressure pushes the liquid into the region of lower pressure.

questions.prompt: Put the crushed-can demonstration in order.
steps: Boil a little water in an open can
Steam pushes most of the air out
Seal the can and plunge it into cold water
Steam condenses; the pressure inside drops
Air pressure outside crushes the can
questions.explain: Low pressure inside + normal air pressure outside = crushed can.

questions.prompt: Air presses on every cm² with about 10 N. What total force does air exert on a notebook cover of 500 cm²?
questions.explain: 10 × 500 = 5000 N, about the weight of 500 kg! It doesn’t crush the book because air pushes equally from below.

questions.prompt: Design an experiment with a plastic bottle to test the hypothesis ‘liquid pressure increases with depth’. Include your variables.
questions.modelAnswer: Make three holes of the same size at different heights on one side of a bottle. Fill it with water to the same level each time and measure how far each jet lands from the bottle with a ruler. Independent variable: depth of the hole below the water surface. Dependent variable: horizontal distance of the jet. Control variables: hole size, liquid, starting water level, same bottle. If the deepest hole squirts furthest, the hypothesis is supported.
rubric: Control variables such as hole size and water level
States what result supports the hypothesis
questions.explain: Criterion B: turn a hypothesis into a testable plan.

questions.text: The pressure exerted by the air around us is called ___ pressure. It is measured with a ___.
questions.explain: Atmospheric pressure is measured with a barometer.

questions.prompt: Why do deep-sea submarines need very thick, strong hulls?
options: Water pressure is enormous at great depths
questions.explain: Pressure increases with depth. At 1 km deep it is about 100 times atmospheric pressure.
